title: Simple code usually wins
explanation: Simple code is easier to debug, easier to maintain, and easier to explain to someone joining the project later.
realExample: When building RyMeds POS counter billing, I chose direct SQL queries over heavy ORM abstractions. This made transaction isolation behavior transparent and prevented implicit database locks.

title: Building is easier than maintaining
explanation: Shipping the first prototype takes days, but maintaining state consistency, handling edge cases, and supporting dependencies takes months.
realExample: In ETLab+, adding real-time lab attendance updates required writing clean unsubscription cleanups; without them, long sessions leaked memory on the browser client.

title: Every bug teaches something deep
explanation: System failures reveal invalid assumptions about memory, network boundaries, timing, or concurrency that documentation alone rarely highlights.
realExample: Spent hours diagnosing MPU-6050 sensor jitter during my robotics internship, which led me to implement software complementary filters to reconcile low-pass accelerometer data with high-pass gyroscope readings.

title: Documentation saves future engineers
explanation: Writing down architectural decisions, schemas, and trade-offs prevents context loss and saves hours when revisiting codebases months later.
realExample: Documenting PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies in ETLab+'s repository enabled rapid testing when modifying tenant permission schemas.

title: Small improvements compound quickly
explanation: Refactoring one component, cleaning one database query, and writing one unit test per day transforms a fragile codebase into a resilient platform.
realExample: Incrementally tuning Ollama model quantization parameters day by day pushed local CPU inference latency from ~2.5 tokens/sec to ~8.5 tokens/sec.

title: Read error messages completely
explanation: The exact line number, call stack, and root failure reason are almost always present in the un-truncated trace if you take time to read it.
realExample: Extracted exact kernel boot failure UUIDs from Arch Linux emergency rescue shells instead of guessing hardware driver flags.

title: Sleep on hard technical problems
explanation: Stepping away from the keyboard allows subconscious pattern recognition to resolve complex bugs far faster than brute-force midnight sessions.
realExample: Discovered the solution to D3 container dynamic resize re-rendering glitches on mobile charts the morning after a stuck late-night debugging session.

title: The best tool is the one you understand
explanation: Reaching for familiar, transparent primitives yields reliable results faster than introducing heavy frameworks with opaque abstraction layers.
realExample: Selected low-overhead FastAPI REST routes paired with SQLite for local memory storage over complex cloud microservice frameworks.
